question: What is a converter dolly, as described in the Connecticut CDL Manual?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig
choice_b: A hydraulic lift used to raise the front of a trailer during loading
choice_c: A brake control device mounted on the tractor dashboard
choice_d: A single-axle trailer used only to carry a spare tire
explanation: A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: If a converter dolly does not have spring brakes, how do you release its brakes before positioning it?
choice_a: By opening the air tank petcock
choice_b: By disconnecting the electrical light cord
choice_c: By pulling the tractor protection valve control
choice_d: By raising the landing gear completely
explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock; if the dolly has spring brakes instead, you would use the dolly parking brake control.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear (second) trailer, what must be true about the trailer's height?
choice_a: It must be exactly level with the center of the dolly's fifth wheel
choice_b: It must be slightly lower than the center of the dolly's fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly as the dolly is pushed under
choice_c: It must be raised well above the dolly's fifth wheel
choice_d: Height does not matter as long as the wheels are chocked
explanation: The trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under it.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: After backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer and before making the visual check, how do you test the coupling?
choice_a: By pulling against the pin (kingpin) of the second semitrailer
choice_b: By driving the rig forward at highway speed
choice_c: By checking the tire pressure of the dolly axle
choice_d: By sounding the horn and listening for an echo
explanation: You test the coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer before making a visual check of the coupling.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: When making a visual check of the converter dolly coupling to the rear trailer, what should you confirm?
choice_a: There is a small visible gap between the upper and lower fifth wheel to allow for movement
choice_b: The locking jaws are closed on the kingpin and there is no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel
choice_c: The tow bar is fully extended and not attached
choice_d: The spare tire mount is empty
explanation: The visual check requires confirming there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel and that the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: After connecting the safety chains, air hoses, and light cords to the second trailer, what should you do next before opening the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer?
choice_a: Close the converter dolly air tank petcock and the shut-off valves at the rear of the second trailer
choice_b: Immediately raise the landing gear all the way and drive off
choice_c: Charge the trailer brakes before closing any valves
choice_d: Re-lock the pintle hook on the first trailer
explanation: After connecting safety chains, air hoses, and light cords, you close the converter dolly air tank petcock and the shut-off valves (service and emergency) at the rear of the second trailer before opening the shut-off valves at the rear of the first trailer.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: After raising the landing gear completely and charging the trailer brakes on a newly coupled double, how do you confirm the brakes will actually work at the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: Check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work
choice_b: Listen for the engine to idle roughly
choice_c: Check that the odometer has reset
choice_d: Confirm the parking brake knob is pulled out
explanation: Push the air supply knob in to charge the trailer brakes, then check for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off; if air pressure is not there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: When uncoupling the rear trailer of a set of twin trailers, when should you chock the wheels of the second trailer?
choice_a: Always, no matter what type of brakes it has
choice_b: If it doesn't have spring brakes
choice_c: Only when parked on a downhill grade
choice_d: Never; chocks are only used on the converter dolly
explanation: As part of uncoupling the rear trailer, you chock the wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Before pulling the converter dolly out from under the rear semitrailer, why do you lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer partway?
choice_a: To make the trailer more visible to other drivers
choice_b: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_c: To automatically release the pintle hook
choice_d: To raise the kingpin above the fifth wheel
explanation: You lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly before pulling the dolly out.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-1

question: Why should you never unlock the pintle hook on the first semitrailer while the converter dolly is still under the rear trailer?
choice_a: It voids the vehicle's manufacturer warranty
choice_b: The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making it very difficult to re-couple
choice_c: It will trigger the trailer's antilock brake warning light
choice_d: It causes the fifth wheel to lock permanently in place
explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer -- the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When coupling a triple-trailer rig, after the tractor is coupled to the first trailer, how do you couple the first trailer to the second trailer?
choice_a: Using the method for coupling doubles, with the converter dolly moved into position
choice_b: By welding a rigid bar between the two trailer frames
choice_c: Using only safety chains, without a fifth wheel or kingpin
choice_d: By backing the tractor into the second trailer at low speed with no dolly
explanation: You move the converter dolly into position and couple the first trailer to the second trailer using the method already described for coupling doubles, completing the triples rig.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, which trailer do you uncouple first?
choice_a: The first trailer, closest to the tractor
choice_b: The third (last) trailer, by pulling the dolly out and unhitching it using the method for uncoupling doubles
choice_c: Whichever trailer is parked closest to a wall
choice_d: All three trailers must be uncoupled at the same time
explanation: You uncouple the third trailer first by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles, before uncoupling the remainder of the rig.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: On a set of doubles or triples, how should the shut-off valves at the rear of the trailers be set?
choice_a: Both the rear of the front trailers and the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
choice_b: The rear of the front trailers should be OPEN; the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED
choice_c: The rear of the front trailers should be CLOSED; the rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
choice_d: Both the rear of the front trailers and the rear of the last trailer should be OPEN
explanation: For double and triple trailers, the shut-off valves at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN, while the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When inspecting the lower fifth wheel on a combination vehicle's coupling system, what should you check regarding the locking jaws?
choice_a: That the locking jaws are around the shank of the kingpin, not the head
choice_b: That the locking jaws are removed entirely for easier coupling
choice_c: That the locking jaws are painted a bright color
choice_d: That the locking jaws are loose enough to allow slight rotation
explanation: When checking the lower fifth wheel, you must confirm the locking jaws are around the shank of the kingpin, not the head, along with no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-2

question: When testing the tractor protection valve on a combination vehicle, what should happen as air pressure in the tanks falls into the manufacturer's specified range (usually 20 to 45 psi)?
choice_a: The trailer air supply control should pop out (or move from normal to emergency position)
choice_b: The parking brakes should automatically release
choice_c: The fifth wheel should unlock automatically
choice_d: The engine should shut off automatically
explanation: The trailer air supply control (tractor protection valve control) should pop out, or move from normal to emergency position, when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually 20 to 45 psi; if it doesn't work properly, a leak could drain all air from the tractor and cause emergency brakes to activate with possible loss of control.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: How do you test that the trailer emergency brakes work on a set of doubles or triples?
choice_a: Charge the trailer air brake system, pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in the emergency position), then pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to confirm the emergency brakes engage
choice_b: Disconnect all air lines and coast downhill in neutral
choice_c: Rev the engine to full throttle while the parking brake is set
choice_d: Check the trailer's tire tread depth
explanation: To test trailer emergency brakes, charge the trailer air brake system and check that the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in the emergency position) and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor to check that the emergency brakes are on.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3

question: When testing trailer service brakes with the hand control (trolley valve) while moving forward slowly, what confirms the trailer brakes are connected and working?
choice_a: You should feel the brakes come on
choice_b: The trailer's turn signals should flash automatically
choice_c: The engine RPM should increase noticeably
choice_d: Nothing should happen, since the trolley valve does not control the trailer brakes
explanation: After checking for normal air pressure and releasing the parking brakes, you move the vehicle forward slowly and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control (trolley valve); you should feel the brakes come on, which tells you the trailer brakes are connected and working.
source_note: Connecticut CDL Manual (R-295 Rev. 12/2024, AAMVA 2022 Modernized CDL Testing System), Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, p. 7-3
